3. `date_of_birth`: DOB 29 February 2000 → "2000-02-29". Note: 2000 is a leap year, so 29 Feb 2000 is valid.

4. `incident_date`: 12 August 2025 → DD/MM/YYYY → "12/08/2025". Note the schema description says ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD but the pattern is DD/MM/YYYY; the instructions say incident_date is DD/MM/YYYY, so follow the instruction and pattern: "12/08/2025".

5. `incident_time`: The document states no time. Instruction 6 says omit this key entirely when the document states no time. So omit.

6. `phone`: 0499 888 777 → E.164 with +61: Australian mobile 0499 888 777 → drop leading 0, add +61 → "+61499888777". Check pattern: ^\+61[0-9]{9}$ → +61 followed by 9 digits: 499888777 is 9 digits. Good.

7. `site`: "cold store 2" — the place where the incident occurred as named in the document. The subject line says "Slip in cold store 2" and body says "cold store 2". So "cold store 2". At most 60 characters — fine.

8. `severity`: No injury, reporter says "Low, in my view". No injury means low is acceptable. Instruction: any injury means at least medium; no injury → low is fine. Reporter says low. So "low".

9. `injury_reported`: false — "No injury."

10. `summary`: restates what happened in the reporter's own words, at most 200 characters. Something like: "Ivy Chen slipped on ice on the floor of cold store 2 but caught the shelving and stayed upright. No injury. Low, in my view, but the floor needs attention."

variant.instructions:
# Incident report form: completion instructions

Read the case document and complete the form.

1. Output a single JSON object containing exactly the keys defined by the form schema, and no other text.
2. `reporter_name` is the full name of the person who made the report, exactly as written in the document.
3. `subject_name` is the full name of the person the incident happened to, exactly as written in the document.
4. `date_of_birth` is the subject's date of birth in ISO 8601 format YYYY-MM-DD.
5. `incident_date` is the date of the incident written as DD/MM/YYYY.
6. `incident_time` is the 24-hour time HH:MM at which the incident occurred; omit this key entirely when the document states no time.
7. `phone` is the reporter's contact number normalised to E.164 with the +61 country code and no spaces or punctuation.
8. `site` is the place where the incident occurred as named in the document, in at most 60 characters.
9. `severity` is one of low, medium, or high: any injury means at least medium, and hospital treatment means high.
10. `injury_reported` is true when the document reports any injury to the subject, otherwise false.
11. `summary` restates what happened in the reporter's own words, in at most 200 characters.
